brief: The Fed raised the federal funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, a hike Allspring says was well telegraphed and largely bond-market driven. Backdrop: Q2 GDP growth of 2.1%, aided by AI build-out, August unemployment at 4.1% (down from a 4.5% November peak), and core PCE at 3.3%, above target since March 2021 and the figure that factored into the decision. Markets now price roughly 100bp of further global tightening over the coming year. Allspring argues fiscal-monetary interplay is narrowing the Fed's flexibility, and expects a fresh rise in energy costs (PPI up 6.6% YoY, crack-spread at a record $59.95/barrel) to offset shelter and core-goods disinflation near term. AI-driven growth carries a capex-slowdown risk and, in Allspring's view, is producing localized bubbles and bond-market crowding within the sector. Response: cautious on longer-duration Treasuries, favoring the 5-10 year belly on attractive real yields, expecting yields to keep rising absent a growth slowdown, while corporate earnings expectations stay robust despite the bond repricing.
